problems.title: The supplementary chord-intersection angle matters
problems.question: Chords AB,CD intersect at M with angle AMC=40°. Arc AD is 20° greater than arc BC. Find arc AD.
problems.idea: The 40° angle uses the other pair of arcs.
formulas: Arc AC+arc BD=2·40°=80°; all four arcs total 360°.
steps: Thus arc AD+arc BC=280°.
Together with their difference 20°, this gives arc AD=(280°+20°)/2.

problems.title: Intersect a line with a piecewise graph
problems.question: Find intersections of y=2x with y=x+7 for x≤6 and y=24−x for x>6.
problems.idea: Check each algebraic root against its branch condition.
steps: x=7 fails the first branch’s x≤6 restriction.
x=8 satisfies the second branch and gives y=16.

problems.title: A sum of two squares becomes one square
problems.question: Find x if (x+3+y)²+(4+x−y)²=−2(x+3+y)(4+x−y).
problems.idea: Move everything left and recognize a square.
steps: Here u+v=2x+7, so (2x+7)²=0.
Thus 2x+7=0; y may be any real number.

problems.title: Parallel and perpendicular parameter lines
problems.question: For which b are 3x+2y−8=0 and 2x−by=2y−5 (a) parallel, (b) perpendicular?
problems.idea: Compare their slopes, treating the vertical special case separately.
formulas: First slope=−3/2; second slope=2/(b+2) when b≠−2.
steps: Parallel slopes require 2/(b+2)=−3/2, giving b=−10/3. Their constants show they are distinct.
Perpendicular slopes require 2/(b+2)=2/3, giving b=1.
b=−2 gives a vertical second line, which satisfies neither condition.

problems.title: Two perpendicular tangent chords
problems.question: Two perpendicular chords of a large circle are tangent to a concentric smaller circle. Each is split by their intersection into lengths 4 and 10. Find the smaller radius.
problems.idea: The centre projects to the midpoint of each chord.
formulas: Each chord has length 14, so its midpoint is 7 from either endpoint.
steps: The intersection is |7−4|=3 from the midpoint along either chord.
Because the chords are perpendicular, that along-chord offset equals the centre’s distance to the other tangent chord.
The distance from the centre to a tangent is the smaller radius.

problems.title: Evaluate shifted inputs of a linear function
problems.question: f(x)=3x−2. Solve f(x)+2f(x−1)=8.
steps: Thus 9x=20.

problems.title: Two horses with interchangeable saddles
problems.question: A good saddle costs 120 lari and a poor saddle 25. Horse 1 with the good saddle costs three times horse 2 with the poor saddle. Horse 2 with the good saddle costs half horse 1 with the poor saddle. Find the horse prices.
steps: The equations simplify to u=3v−45 and u=2v+215.
Equating gives v=260. Then u=735.

problems.title: Tangency lengths in an isosceles triangle
problems.question: AB=BC and the incircle touches AB at M. BM is 1 cm longer than base AC; the perimeter is 23 cm. Find AC.
problems.idea: The tangent segments from a base vertex equal half the base.
formulas: Let base b and each leg l. Then BM=l−b/2=b+1.
steps: Thus l=3b/2+1.
The perimeter gives 2l+b=4b+2=23.

problems.title: A system with one extra linear condition
problems.question: Find a such that the solution of 2(x+a)+3y=x−2 and 2(y−a)+x=10−x also satisfies 3x−2y=5.
problems.idea: Solve the system in terms of a first.
steps: Subtract to obtain y=−(7+3a)/2, then x=(17+5a)/2.
The extra condition gives (65+21a)/2=5.
Thus 21a=−55.

problems.title: An altitude projection determines the acute angles
problems.question: In right triangle ABC, CD is the altitude to hypotenuse AB, and BD−DA=AC. Find its acute angles.
formulas: Let DA=m,BD=n,AC=c. Then c²=m(m+n) and n=m+c.
steps: Substitute n=m+c: c²=2m²+mc. Dividing by c² gives 2(m/c)²+m/c−1=0.
The positive solution is m/c=1/2; the negative solution is impossible for a length.
Then AB=m+n=2m+c=2c, so AC is half the hypotenuse.
The angle opposite AC is 30°, and the other acute angle is 60°.
